source: make a shooting game with a sliding,crouching, dashing mechanics and include assault rifles, snipers, revolvers, shotguns, pistols and make them do a fair amount of damage each and make a battle arena for ppl to fight in and if u die I respawn and first person to get the most kills wins and each kill gives the player 10 coins and coins will be used to open weapon boxes and each win gives 50 coins and the weapon boxes will cost 150 coin and the players with fight for 2 minutes and 30 seconds

image_prompt.text: Fixed-position armour and weapon pickups on a respawn timer that players fight to control
Raised nests and platforms reached by exposed stairs, giving the snipers and revolvers a firing position
Rooms and corridors with two or more ways in and out, so the arena keeps players circulating instead of dead-ending
Respawn points around the arena with geometry breaking the sightlines into them

layout_placement.text: Timed armour and weapon spawns at fixed points
Respawn points distributed around the arena so a player killed mid-round re-enters away from the fight that killed them
an enclosed battle arena boundary keeping the fight inside for the 2 minute 30 second round

notes: Preset caveat: Arena Deathmatch supplies map weapon pickups, but this prompt's weapons come from boxes bought with coins. The pickups are kept per batch policy and are in conflict with the stated acquisition loop.
cover-elevated carries P0 + tiered, and would become P2 if any nest overhangs the floor below.
Sliding, crouching and dashing change what spacing is legal in this arena, and there is no field to tell the generator that.

open_questions.ask: No look was stated - military, sci-fi, or bright and arcade?
How many players fight at once? A 2:30 free-for-all plays very differently at 6 players than at 20, and that sets the arena size.

coverage_missing.ask: What should the arena look like? Nothing in the prompt says.
How many players per match? That is what sizes the arena.
Is it free-for-all or teams? 'First person to get the most kills' reads free-for-all, but the arena is built differently either way.
How far does the dash go? Dash distance changes the legal gap between platforms and cover.

answers.ask: No look was stated - military, sci-fi, or bright and arcade?
answers.answer: Use a military-themed battle arena with clear, practical cover and readable weapon designs.

answers.ask: How many players fight at once? A 2:30 free-for-all plays very differently at 6 players than at 20, and that sets the arena size.
answers.answer: Make it a 6-player free-for-all so the arena can stay compact and fast-paced.
